evidence.claim: U.S. electricity demand growth is structurally supported by data-center expansion, with IEA projecting nearly 2% annual U.S. electricity demand growth through 2030 and about half of the total increase driven by data centers.

Interconnection and grid congestion are material chokepoints, with Berkeley Lab reporting about 10,300 active U.S. interconnection projects at the end of 2024, representing around 1,400 GW of generation and 890 GW of storage.
evidence.source_title: Queued Up: 2025 Edition, Characteristics of Power Plants Seeking Transmission Interconnection As of the End of 2024

evidence.claim: EIA's May 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook forecasts U.S. electricity demand to rise 1.3% in 2026 to almost 4,250 billion kWh and grow another 3.1% in 2027.
Constellation announced a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to support the launch of the Crane Clean Energy Center and restart of Three Mile Island Unit 1.
evidence.source_title: Constellation to Launch Crane Clean Energy Center, Restoring Jobs and Carbon-Free Power to The Grid

evidence.claim: Talen announced that it expanded its nuclear energy relationship with Amazon to provide carbon-free energy from the Susquehanna nuclear power plant to AWS data centers in the region.
evidence.source_title: Talen Energy SEC Filing / Press Release: Talen Energy Expands Nuclear Energy Relationship with Amazon

evidence.claim: Talen's 2026 filing states that, at full contract quantity, it will provide AWS with 1,920 MW of carbon-free nuclear power through 2042, while FERC rehearing remains a pending regulatory item.

GE Vernova's Q1 2026 materials reported gas-power equipment backlog and slot-reservation agreements growing from 83 GW to 100 GW, and $2.4 billion of Electrification equipment orders to support data centers.
evidence.source_title: GE Vernova reports first quarter 2026 financial results and raises 2026 guidance

evidence.claim: Eaton's Q1 2026 analyst presentation reported total backlog growth of 44% in Electrical Americas, 73% in Electrical Global, and Electrical Americas data-center orders up approximately 240%.

Quanta Services reported Q1 2026 revenues of $7.87 billion, remaining performance obligations of $26.2 billion, total backlog of $48.5 billion, and increased substantially all 2026 financial expectations.
evidence.source_title: Quanta Services Reports First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: AEP's Q1 2026 release says new load additions expand to 63 GW by 2030 and the company increased its five-year capital plan while reaffirming 2026 operating earnings guidance.
evidence.source_url: Cached evidence referenced; full URL not available in provided excerpt

evidence.claim: EIA forecasts U.S. natural gas consumption by the electric power sector to remain near recent highs in summer 2026 and set a record in summer 2027.
evidence.source_title: Natural gas for power generation flat this summer, record high expected in 2027 - EIA

falsification_plan.node: Firm carbon-free power and nuclear PPAs
watch_items: Failure or delay of nuclear restart milestones
FERC or regional grid rulings that weaken co-located or front-of-meter economics
Hyperscalers choosing cheaper intermittent renewables plus storage instead of premium firm nuclear contracts
Nuclear operating or capex overruns that dilute contract economics
Backlog cancellations
Lead-time normalization faster than expected
Margin pressure from supply-chain or warranty issues
Policy restrictions on gas-fired generation for data centers
Utility capex deferrals
Customer deposit requirements reducing speculative data-center load queues
Labor constraints hurting project margins
Regulators disallowing cost recovery for large-load infrastructure

falsification_plan.node: Electrical distribution and data-center power conversion
watch_items: Backlog-to-revenue conversion slowing
Data-center order growth decelerating
New supplier capacity reducing lead times and pricing power
AI capex digestion cycles causing order pauses

falsification_plan.node: Downstream data-center developers and powered land
watch_items: Power procurement delays
Rising financing costs or capex intensity
Hyperscaler self-build reducing third-party demand
Lease pricing failing to offset higher power and infrastructure costs

memory_update.content: Layer 3 top research priorities: CEG, GEV, PWR, AEP, TLN, ETN. Primary chokepoints: firm carbon-free power, gas turbine slots, grid construction/interconnection, switchgear/electrical distribution, and regulated utility large-load conversion.
Downstream data-center REITs are relevant mapping candidates but ranked below power/grid/equipment chokepoints because their economics may be constrained by the scarce upstream nodes.

Key falsifiers: regulatory rejection of nuclear/data-center structures, weak contracted quality of utility load pipelines, rapid normalization of turbine/switchgear lead times, and customer-funded infrastructure terms proving less favorable than expected.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need continued verification of restart execution, regulatory milestones, final capital cost, nuclear operating risk, and whether incremental hyperscaler PPAs are signed at similarly attractive economics.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Closest large-cap public-market exposure to the firm carbon-free power chokepoint. Existing nuclear generation is scarce, difficult to replicate, slow to permit, and directly relevant to hyperscaler demand for 24/7 clean power. The Microsoft-linked Three Mile Island Unit 1 / Crane Clean Energy Center PPA provides unusually direct evidence that AI/cloud demand can translate into long-duration nuclear contracting.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need more source-backed confirmation of AI/data-center-specific contracting, regional basis exposure, capacity-market upside, fuel-price sensitivity, and whether market pricing already discounts firm-power scarcity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: High-priority firm-power candidate because it combines nuclear, gas, retail power, and capacity-market exposure. It is less pure than Constellation but potentially benefits from the same scarcity of dispatchable generation and rising load growth in power-constrained regions.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need diligence on backlog quality, margin conversion, slot-reservation economics, turbine delivery timing, warranty/quality risk, and whether orders are incremental AI/data-center demand or broader power-cycle recovery.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Equipment-side bottleneck candidate with exposure to gas turbines, grid equipment, and electrification systems. If new firm-power additions are constrained by turbine slots and grid equipment availability, GE Vernova sits near a scarce supply-chain node rather than only downstream demand.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need segmentation of backlog tied specifically to data-center and utility interconnection demand, labor availability, project-margin durability, and exposure to any utility capex deferrals.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Cross-cutting grid-construction bottleneck candidate. If deliverable power, substations, transmission, and distribution upgrades are the real chokepoint, Quanta benefits across utilities, renewables, large-load interconnections, data centers, and grid-hardening cycles.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to verify contracted quality of the 63 GW load pipeline, deposit/take-or-pay structures, regulatory treatment, customer credit quality, and whether grid constraints delay energization.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Regulated-utility candidate with large disclosed load-addition pipeline and direct exposure to transmission ownership, large-load service agreements, and customer-funded infrastructure. Strong candidate for studying whether AI/data-center demand converts into rate-base growth rather than only headline load requests.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current load-forecast filings, approved capital plans, large-load tariff treatment, political risk around customer cost allocation, and whether required generation/transmission buildout is approved on attractive terms.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: High-priority regulated utility because Virginia is a key U.S. data-center load region. Dominion is a direct way to research whether data-center concentration creates rate-base growth, transmission/substation buildout, and generation additions.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need close monitoring of FERC/regional-grid rulings, interconnection agreement treatment, power-delivery structure, capacity-market implications, and whether AWS contract economics offset regulatory complexity.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Very pure nuclear/data-center power candidate due to the AWS/Susquehanna relationship. It ranks slightly below the larger and more diversified firm-power names because regulatory uncertainty around co-located and front-of-meter structures is unusually thesis-critical.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need to separate AI/data-center orders from broader electrical-cycle strength, track lead times, pricing, backlog cancellation risk, and margin sustainability as capacity expands.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Electrical-equipment bottleneck candidate. Switchgear, medium-voltage distribution, power conversion, and data-center electrical systems are required to turn utility capacity into usable compute capacity. Eaton's reported backlog and data-center order growth make this a strong evidence-backed node.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that AI power/cooling demand continues to outgrow competition and that margins remain durable despite capacity additions, customer concentration, and rapid technology changes in liquid cooling.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Highly pure exposure to data-center critical power, thermal management, and liquid-cooling infrastructure. It is close to the operating-data-center conversion bottleneck, though supplier scarcity may be lower than nuclear assets, turbine slots, or utility interconnection capacity.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need confirmation of customer-funded infrastructure terms, commission approvals, timing of required generation additions, load ramp schedule, and whether political/regulatory risk limits allowed returns.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Regulated-utility candidate with visible hyperscale demand in Louisiana, including Meta-related load. It is useful for studying how data-center load converts into generation, transmission, and distribution investment under regulated utility frameworks.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need current Georgia Power and broader Southern load forecasts, data-center customer disclosures, tariff filings, capex approvals, and clarity on whether incremental demand earns acceptable regulated returns.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Relevant regulated-utility exposure to Southeast economic development, data-center load, large-load tariffs, and utility capex. Ranked below AEP, Dominion, and Entergy because the cached evidence is less specific to a clearly quantified AI/data-center chokepoint.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that AI/data-center customers contract incremental renewable-plus-storage capacity on attractive terms and that transmission/interconnection constraints do not dilute project economics.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Second-order clean-power and utility-infrastructure candidate. Renewables, storage, corporate PPAs, and FPL load growth are relevant, but the Serenity priority is lower because intermittent clean power is less directly scarce than firm nuclear, gas turbines, interconnection capacity, or grid construction.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need verification of powered-land inventory, megawatt delivery timelines, lease economics, hyperscaler demand durability, and financing/capex burden.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Useful downstream mapping candidate for powered land, data-center capacity, tenant demand, and utility commitments. Ranked below power and grid suppliers because downstream data-center owners may be constrained by the very power bottlenecks that upstream suppliers monetize.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence of AI-specific utilization, power availability by market, on-site generation economics, customer contract duration, and whether capex intensity offsets demand growth.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Relevant AI-ready colocation and interconnection candidate, with potential exposure to on-site power and alternative power procurement. Ranked as a customer/developer mapping name rather than a primary chokepoint owner.

ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need direct evidence that data-center power materially affects gas volumes, margins, or contracted power economics relative to Chevron's overall business scale.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Lower-priority second-order exposure through natural gas supply, behind-the-meter generation, and data-center power partnerships. It is thematically relevant but public-market purity is low because Chevron's equity story is still dominated by integrated oil and gas fundamentals.

scoring_notes.bottleneck_severity: How hard the relevant node is to expand, permit, interconnect, construct, or substitute.
scoring_notes.demand_durability: Persistence and visibility of end-market demand linked to AI/data-center load, electrification, utility capex, and power demand.
scoring_notes.evidence_quality: Strength of source-backed evidence from filings, company disclosures, official agencies, and primary materials.
scoring_notes.falsifiability: Clarity of observable events that could confirm or disprove the thesis.
scoring_notes.mispricing_potential: Research hypothesis that market may underappreciate the chokepoint; not a price forecast.
scoring_notes.public_market_purity: How directly the listed company maps to the chokepoint versus having diluted exposure.
scoring_notes.risk_clarity: How clearly regulatory, execution, customer, commodity, financing, and valuation risks can be monitored.
scoring_notes.score_scale: 0 = no meaningful support; 1 = weak; 2 = emerging; 3 = credible but incomplete; 4 = strong; 5 = very strong
scoring_notes.supplier_scarcity: Degree to which few public companies control the scarce asset, equipment slot, or delivery capability.

selected_for_brief_generation.brief_reason: Purest large-cap firm carbon-free power chokepoint with direct hyperscaler PPA evidence.
Scarce equipment node across gas turbines, electrification, and grid equipment.
Cross-cutting grid construction and substation/transmission bottleneck.
Regulated-utility test case for large-load service agreements and rate-base conversion.
High-purity nuclear/data-center thesis with clear regulatory falsification points.
Electrical distribution and switchgear bottleneck with strong backlog evidence.

summary: Layer 3 prioritizes Energy-theme candidates by Serenity chokepoint logic: start with durable electricity demand, then rank exposure to hard-to-build firm power, grid interconnection, transmission/substation construction, electrical equipment, and data-center power conversion. Highest-priority research candidates are not necessarily the most obvious downstream data-center names; they are the public companies closest to scarce firm power, scarce grid delivery capacity, or equipment/construction bottlenecks with strong evidence and clear falsification paths. This is research prioritization only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
